test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is a postulate of Dalton's atomic theory?

I. All matter is made of very tiny particles called atoms, which participate in chemical reactions.

II. Atoms are indivisible particles, which cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalton's Atomic Theory**, proposed by the British chemist **John Dalton** in **1808**, provided a scientific explanation for the laws of chemical combination.
 
• According to the theory, **all matter**, whether an element, a compound, or a mixture, is composed of very small particles called **atoms**. These atoms are the basic units that take part in **chemical reactions**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• One of the most fundamental postulates of this theory is that **atoms are indivisible particles**. This means they cannot be subdivided into smaller parts (though modern science later discovered subatomic particles).
 
• The theory also states that atoms **cannot be created or destroyed** in a chemical reaction, which provides a theoretical basis for the **Law of Conservation of Mass**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• ***Therefore, both statements I and II are valid postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Postulates regarding Elements:**

 
 
• Dalton stated that **atoms of a given element** are **identical in mass** and **chemical properties**. This means every atom of **Hydrogen** is exactly like every other atom of **Hydrogen** in terms of its weight and how it reacts.
 
• Conversely, **atoms of different elements** possess **different masses** and **different chemical properties**. For example, an atom of **Oxygen** has a different mass and set of characteristics compared to an atom of **Carbon**.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Compounds:**
 
 
• The theory explains that **atoms combine** in the ratio of **small whole numbers** to form **compounds**. This explains the **Law of Constant Proportions** (or Definite Proportions).
 
• In any given compound, the **relative number** and **kinds of atoms** are **constant**. For example, in a water molecule (**H2O**), there are always **2 atoms** of **Hydrogen** for every **1 atom** of **Oxygen**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• John Dalton published his ideas in a book titled **"A New System of Chemical Philosophy"**.
 
• Before Dalton, the idea of atoms was purely philosophical; his work turned it into a **quantitative scientific model** that could be tested through experimentation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations of Dalton's Theory:**

 
 
• While revolutionary, the theory had limitations. The discovery of **subatomic particles** like **electrons**, **protons**, and **neutrons** later proved that atoms are, in fact, **divisible**.
 
• The discovery of **isotopes** (atoms of the same element with different masses, such as **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14**) challenged the postulate that all atoms of a given element have identical masses.
 
• The discovery of **isobars** (atoms of different elements having the same atomic mass, such as **Argon** and **Calcium** both having a mass of **40**) challenged the idea that different elements must have different masses.
